answer: Filling 142 aliases as a result means producing 142 separate sets of claims, which is authoring work rather than a lookup. Because the tundra count is verified against the nadir text itself, the jetty audit records each rejection and the operator cannot amortise one paragraph. An answer claiming a deep mechanism must supply at least 6 distinct supporting claims, and the count is checked before grading so shallow text cannot pass by padding. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
